original_test_intent: Verify that the intended board FRU reports the approved board product/model designation and that the same product identity appears in the authoritative BMC UI/OEM API.
original_method: Bind the board FRU and UI/API resource to the same hardware, retrieve both raw product strings securely, apply only approved model aliases and revision handling, and compare against the versioned board BOM/product recipe.
manual_activity: Supply the authoritative board product/model, approved aliases/revision suffix rules and FRU-to-OEM/UI mapping; no physical activity or mutation is needed.
required_inputs: Validated OEM/UI or Redfish board source
safety_requirements: Use read-only FRU and API operations
Never write FRU or issue raw mutation/PATCH/board control
Do not substitute board part number for product name
Stop on multiple boards or ambiguous model identity
agent_execution_scope: Bind the intended board FRU record
Resolve the validated OEM/UI product source
Capture complete redacted evidence and statuses
Compare with the BOM product oracle
Report exact match, mismatch or ambiguity

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `ipmitool fru print` can expose Board Product, but the assumed `.Board.ProductName` property and chassis member are not validated. A raw match or missing-path fallback lacks the BOM and revision semantics needed for the criterion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use secure read-only access to capture the bound board FRU and validated OEM/UI product property, retain raw strings, apply the approved product alias/revision mapping and compare with the BOM product/model.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The `ipmitool fru list` inspection, Board Product field, UI agreement criterion and 2/0-minute timing are preserved; property, alias rules and expected product are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a three-way product-identity comparator that records board provenance, raw product strings, model/revision tokens, alias-policy version and canonical result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces an informal visual comparison and guessed property with an auditable model identity tied to the BOM.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Adds detection of wrong model, unauthorized alias and revision mismatch while retaining read-only FRU/UI comparison.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Product labels may be marketing aliases or include revision text; overly broad canonicalization can incorrectly accept a different board family.

project_override_considerations: `Board Product` is a model/product designation, not the adjacent part number or manufacturer. Private script content is unavailable and cannot supply implicit alias rules.
expected_evidence: Complete redacted FRU output and status
Resolved OEM/UI product source and response status
Raw FRU and UI product strings
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master and prior reviews consistently target the Board Product value. DeepSeek's unvalidated endpoint and absent BOM oracle are incomplete execution details rather than conflicting source meaning.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The product/model field and comparison goal are clear. The BOM oracle, alias rules and source mapping are finite project packages.

review_improvement: Prevents a guessed API property, marketing alias or silently ignored revision from being accepted as proof that the correct board product is programmed.
independent_technical_reasoning: Board Product conveys model identity and may legitimately differ from a numeric part number or legal manufacturer string. A UI can display a marketing name while FRU stores an engineering model, so comparison requires a narrowly approved alias and revision map. At the same time, collapsing different model suffixes can hide a wrong board population. Because the data can be safely read once those project inputs are supplied, REQUIRES is the correct boundary.
